extracted.intended_audience: patent proprietors, potential opponents, patent attorneys and litigation practitioners (clients of IP law firms)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules, timelines and strategic considerations for initiating, conducting and appealing oppositions against European patents before the EPO (Opposition Division and Boards of Appeal). Aimed at parties and their representatives involved in EPO oppositions and parallel national infringement/invalidity actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition filing period
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition proceedings may be initiated against a European patent within nine months after publication of the mention of its grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No legal interest of the opponent has to be proven; an opposition may be filed by any natural or legal person, including a 'straw man' acting for an unknown third person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any natural or legal person may file an opposition; a 'straw man' (person without real interest) is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions are typically filed in reaction to national infringement actions but are often filed as precautionary measures due to relatively low costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for revocation (permissible grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent may only be opposed on the grounds that: the subject-matter of one or more of the claims is not patentable (in particular not novel or not inventive); the patent does not disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art; and the subject-matter of the patent extends beyond the content of the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the exclusive substantive grounds on which an opposition can be based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other grounds not admissible
rubrics_metrics.description: Other grounds of opposition are not admissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of inadmissible grounds: lack of clarity of claim wording, or allegations that the invention was 'stolen' from the opponent or a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raising grounds within opposition period and new grounds after expiry
rubrics_metrics.description: The grounds of opposition must be raised by an opponent before the expiry of the opposition period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction of new grounds after the expiry is subject to procedural restrictions: in first instance a new ground may be examined if considered prima facie relevant by the Examining Division; otherwise admission is limited and discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-instance deadlines and exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: After expiry of the opposition period, the EPO sets a four-month deadline for the proprietor to respond to the opposition(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may be invited to submit further replies within specified time limits. Most opposition cases may be expected to be decided in first instance in less than 18 months; written exchange of briefs occurs during this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings and preliminary opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested by at least one party, the Opposition Division summons the parties to oral proceedings; the summons includes a non-binding preliminary opinion of the Opposition Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preliminary opinion indicates issues considered relevant and may include a preliminary assessment of the case. Oral proceedings typically take one or sometimes two days (video conferencing rules may apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of Opposition Division
rubrics_metrics.description: An Opposition Division generally consists of three technically qualified members; the Division may be enlarged by a legal member if complex legal questions are to be decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legal member is generally called upon for taking evidence on alleged prior public use or other legal complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of examination limited to opposed subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The Opposition Division considers the legal questions of the case and evaluates the facts on its own motion (ex officio) but is bound to the extent to which the patent has been opposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the opposition attacks only certain independent claims, other independent claims of the granted patent are not to be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence disclosure and timing (opponents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opponents should cite all known evidence and, in particular, all known prior art against the patent under opposition before the expiry of the opposition period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After expiration of the opposition period, admission of new facts and evidence is at the discretion of the Opposition Division, primarily exercised on the basis of relevance; discretion is exercised more restrictively after deadlines set in the summons to oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to the patent (limits and requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent proprietor may defend the opposed patent as granted or in a limited version. Amendments may be chosen from the whole content of the original patent application’s disclosure as long as the scope of protection is not extended beyond the granted patent’s scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments of the patent need to be occasioned by a ground of opposition; opposition proceedings must not be used to reformulate claims or description for clarity or cosmetic reasons or to adapt them to competitors' embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary requests and admissibility of new requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent proprietor may defend the patent in different versions on the basis of a main request and one or more auxiliary requests; an auxiliary request is considered only under the condition that the main request or a higher auxiliary request is found not to meet EPC requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of new requests is procedurally limited. Requests submitted in oral proceedings are, as a rule, not admitted unless they can be readily discussed by the panel and the opponent, or if they react to a new objection in oral proceedings. Primarily only small, editorial amendments may be made during oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition Division decision outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the oral proceedings the Opposition Division deliberates and issues its decision: either a full revocation of the patent, a limitation, or the maintenance of the patent as granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are issued after deliberation by the panel; pandemic-related adjustments (video conferences) may affect format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal time limits and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party adversely affected by the decision of the Opposition Division may appeal within two months after receipt of the written decision; the appellant has an additional two months to submit their reasoning. Time limits are not extendible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement of grounds of appeal shall contain the appellant’s complete case, including all legal and technical arguments as well as any modified main and auxiliary requests. Appeals may be rejected as inadmissible if they do not deal with the appealed decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boards of Appeal admission discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: In appeal proceedings, the Boards of Appeal exercise their discretion to admit new facts, evidence or requests considering the relevance of the submissions, their complexity, the current state of the proceedings and the need for procedural economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that could have been made or were rejected in first instance may be rejected; late submissions requiring cancelling/postponement of oral proceedings are generally not admitted. Boards tend to act as reviewing bodies and are increasingly strict about arguments that put the case on a new footing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of important legal questions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Technical Board of Appeal may refer, on its own motion or on request of a party, a question of law to the Enlarged Board of Appeal to ensure uniform application of the law or if an important point of law arises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral is exceptional and used to ensure consistent legal interpretation across cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural language and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party may use any of the three official languages of the EPO (English, German or French). Oral proceedings are held in the language of the proceedings (the language in which the application resulting in the opposed patent was published).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party may express itself in any official language and interpretation between the three official languages is provided at no extra cost on prior request. Communications and final decisions are issued in the language of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of experts and evidentiary practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition Divisions and Boards decide opposition cases based on their own technical expertise; appointment of an expert ex officio is rarely ordered. Parties may present their own private experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private experts may submit opinions in writing and, upon prior notice to the EPO, may present at oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation before the EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may be represented by a professional representative admitted to practice before the EPO, in particular by a European Patent Attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponents and proprietors commonly use professional representatives; coordination between patent attorneys and attorneys-at-law may be important in parallel national infringement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawal of opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Although an opponent may withdraw the opposition at any time, such withdrawal does not necessarily terminate the opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Opposition Division may continue the proceedings on its own motion and issue a decision within the framework of the original opposition. Withdrawal of the (only) appeal will, however, terminate second-instance appeal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention by defendants in parallel infringement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A defendant in patent infringement proceedings may intervene in pending opposition proceedings within three months from the institution of infringement proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The defendant is obliged to accept the opposition proceedings in the stage they are in but may introduce new grounds of opposition and submit new facts and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic considerations: national invalidity vs opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no pending opposition procedure, the defendant in infringement proceedings needs to consider whether an opposition within the nine-month period should be initiated or whether national invalidity proceedings should be started against the national part of the patent being enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: German Federal Patent Court may apply a somewhat higher inventive-step hurdle than the EPO, but revocation actions in Germany are only possible if no opposition is pending at the EPO. Early coordination with competitors and strategic planning are advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of national infringement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In Germany, patent infringement proceedings may be stayed at the request of the defendant if the infringement court considers it very likely that the patent will be revoked in the opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision to stay is discretionary for the national court and has no binding or prejudicial effect on the EPO opposition decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation and apportionment
rubrics_metrics.description: In European opposition proceedings, each party generally bears its own costs, including official fees for filing the opposition or an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An apportionment of costs may exceptionally be ordered, particularly in cases of abuse of procedure where an adversary had to bear superfluous costs (e.g., failure to inform EPO of non-representation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revalidation and translation costs after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a European patent has been maintained in opposition proceedings in amended form, it must be revalidated in all designated states, requiring submission of a translation of the granted patent in which it was initially validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revalidation leads to additional costs to maintain protection in designated states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial effects of opposition decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision in opposition proceedings is retroactively effective in all states where the opposed patent is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By contrast, national patent invalidity proceedings (the only option after the opposition period or a terminated opposition) may lead to differing results from country to country.
